analysis:
The PR widens inline-video MIME admission in MediaIngest.swift (head lines 769-777 and 798-801). The admitted headers are now data:video/mp4, data:video/x-m4v, data:video/quicktime and data:video/mov with ;base64. Matching is a case-insensitive set lookup on the lowercased header, equivalent to the prior caseInsensitiveCompare. The comment states that MemoryBackedVideoAsset sniffs the container from the bytes, so the MIME label is not trusted for format.

The http(s), file and other MIME schemes remain rejected because the guard is exact-set membership. dataFromDataURI is still invoked with maxMediaDecodedBytes, so the existing caps still apply. No file-write path is introduced, so T-050 mitigations are preserved. The threat-model doc update at head lines 1969-1970 aligns T-050 with this behavior.

The libs/mlx-swift-lm submodule bump (7bed821 -> 54227ba) is opaque. Its contents are not supplied, and per the comment it likely carries the byte-sniffing logic in MemoryBackedVideoAsset. Integration and deeper review should verify three things:
- the sniffing accepts only MP4/QuickTime ftyp/moov structures;
- AVURLAssetReferenceRestrictions.forbidAll is still set;
- no temp-file or URL path was added (T-050 detection_hint).

Widening the label set does not expand parser surface if sniffing gates AVFoundation to the same container types. However, sniffing could relax the previous label-based restriction if the submodule now admits other containers.

The remaining doc units (T-041 detection hint through T-058) are unchanged context with no security drift.
